asks: a shortfall spreads out from a body. How does what reaches a distance depend on that distance, and on what else?

steps.via: every rule is a function of its own match
steps.line: \delta \text{ is conserved on its way out}
working: every one of the 7 terms the line carries is a rule acting on the match it was handed
none of them consults anything outside it, so agreement is carried and disagreement is only moved
the DENSITY is pushed back at a = 2 \sigma F \rho + -\paren{\nu \paren{0 - \bar{DEG} \paren{\rho^{\paren{\bar{DEG} - 1}}}}}, which is a different quantity
steps.because: a rule reads the refs its match handed over and nothing else, so two worlds that agree about a match agree after it - a difference between them can be moved and cannot be made or unmade. What a meeting takes from the disturbed world it leaves as a hole in the undisturbed one, and the difference is the same size. So as much of the shortfall crosses a far shell as a near one, which is what the dilution argument wants

working: exits(p): DEG ways out, none of them special
steps.because: a point's exits are alike and a rule reads none of them by name, so what leaves a place goes every way alike

steps.via: how many places are r steps out
working: exits(p): the ways out of a point, DEG of them
steps: where one exit leads - and that is all the rules say about where anything is
D of those ways are independent, so places within r steps ∝ r^{D}
steps.because: the rules give a point, DEG ways out of it, and where each one leads - and nothing else about where anything is. So how far is how many steps were taken, and how many places are that far out is a count of walks. D is how many of those ways are independent, so within r steps there are r choices along each of D and the places within r go as r^{D}; the places at exactly r are the difference between two of those, which is r^{D-1}. Every step is whole and every place counted once, so this is the count itself and not an approximation to one

working: the choice is 1 way straight on against n_{f} folded
steps.because: the turn draws one way straight on against the folded ways of the place, so the share of a step that carried a ray on is one against one plus the record

working: and it dwells 1/v there, with v = \frac{1}{\paren{1 + n_{f}}}
steps.because: count what crosses a shell in one tick - the sites on it, times what is at each, times the share of a step that went outward - and MOVEMENT neither makes nor destroys, so that count is carried outward unchanged. So what CROSSES one site is the whole of it over the number of sites there are at that distance. What IS at one site is that again over how fast a share gets across

steps.via: what is pushed back is screened
steps.because: nothing in the line pushes δ back, so the chance of surviving one step is one and the chance of surviving r of them is one. What is left at r is what spread there, and the dilution is the whole of the law
